# /quenching-align — the one door of every front

**Launcher.** On POSIX the skill calls `cq`; on Windows it calls `cq.cmd`, the sibling the deploy installs beside `bin/cq`.

**Input**: `$ARGUMENTS` — an optional flow, `status`, then an optional front. `align` is the
default flow; a front is an argument, never a skill of its own.

| Input | Flow |
| --- | --- |
| *(empty)* or `<front>` | **align** — converge every applicable front, or only the named one |
| `status` or `status <front>` | **status** — the read-only report of every front, or only the named one, plus the security audit |

The fronts are `knowledge`, `design`, `components`, `ops`, `proof`, `toolchain`, `delivery` and
`opensource`; `security` is a status-only front. A first word that is neither `status` nor a front
is a scope (a path inside a front), and the flow is `align`.

## Where a front's text lives

Each front's text lives in a reference its own module installs, never in a skill of its own:
`.agents/quenching/references/<front>-align/align.md` and `…/status.md` (`security` has the latter
only), with its bands and contracts beside them. A front whose module is not installed has no
folder: it is `not-installed: <module>`. The `knowledge` status is the `status` flow of
`/quenching-knowledge`, run inline; the `components` align carries the `harness-align` step (`.agents/quenching/references/components-align/harness-align.md`).

**Following a front.** Read its reference whole, once, and follow it inline, with the same inherited
authorization and the same stages; its `cq <front> …` verbs run as written, each cited as the
`quenching` MCP tool per
[tool-resolution.md](.agents/quenching/references/align/tool-resolution.md) §Resolving the tool.

## Execution order

This table is the **one executable declaration** of the local-front order. The `Depends on`
column is a dependency edge, not a display ordinal: a later front is never run before the front
named in that cell has completed its inherited authorization.

| Front | Reference | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `knowledge` — `/docs/` | `.agents/quenching/references/knowledge-align/align.md` | applicability |
| `design` — `/.design/` | `.agents/quenching/references/design-align/align.md` | `knowledge` |
| `components` — `.agents/` and the Claude bridge | `.agents/quenching/references/components-align/align.md` | `design` |
| `ops` — operations surface | `.agents/quenching/references/ops-align/align.md` | `components` |
| `proof` — verification surface | `.agents/quenching/references/proof-align/align.md` | `ops` |
| `toolchain` — toolchain surface | `.agents/quenching/references/toolchain-align/align.md` | `proof` |
| `delivery` — delivery surface | `.agents/quenching/references/delivery-align/align.md` | `toolchain` |
| `opensource` — community, license and governance artifacts | `.agents/quenching/references/opensource-align/align.md` | `delivery` |

**Only deployed modules are conducted.** Before the first front, read `cq modules --json` once
([tool-resolution.md](.agents/quenching/references/align/tool-resolution.md) §Routing into
another module). A front whose module reports `enabled: false` is `not-installed: <module>`: it is
skipped, named in the report, and its dependants depend on the nearest earlier front that ran.

The `specs` provider flow has no row because it owns no local tree, and the `git` pillar has none
because it answers live questions without a converging front tree. `security` has no align: it is
read in the status flow only.

Every applicable front must expose the common front mold at
`.agents/quenching/references/front-align/mold.md`. The conductor sequences and reports;
it never reimplements a front's verifier or repair logic.

Before probing, read `specs_read(verb="config")`. An absent `shared.profiles.installed` means all eight
local fronts are eligible; a declared list limits the conductor to its named local fronts, in the
dependency order above. Report other local fronts as skipped by profile. This scope affects only
this conductor run: it does not remove commands or change a command's own invocation contract.

## Workflow

The **align** flow, and the default.

### Applicability

Probe every declared front in the table before inventory. If `$ARGUMENTS` names a front or a path
inside one, probe only that front and mark the others skipped by scope.

- **`knowledge`** — run `knowledge_read(verb="validate")`; record the bundle, validator counts,
  project memory and harness files.
- **`design`** — run `design_read(verb="status")` when installed; when absent, run
  `design align --check --json` only when scope or root `PRODUCT.md`/`DESIGN.md` artifacts signal
  adoption.
- **`components`** — run `components_read(verb="doctor")`, `components_write(verb="migrate")`
  and `components_write(verb="bridge", check=true)`; inspect command skills for legacy pairs.
  `migrate` exit 1 puts its whole plan (operations, renames, conflicts) in the Authorization plan
  as one block; `bridge --check` exit 1 puts its changes there. Conformant is `migrate`
  `conformant: true` and `bridge --check` exit 0.
- **`ops`** — read `.agents/quenching.json` (legacy: `.agents/quenching.json`)
  for `ops.opsRoot`; when absent, inspect only
  `scripts/`, `tools/`, `bin/` and `script/` for an executable entry point.
- **`proof`** — read `.agents/quenching.json` (legacy: `.agents/quenching.json`)
  for `proof.proofRoot`; when absent, inspect only
  `tests/` and `test/` for a test module.
- **`toolchain`** — run `toolchain_read(verb="doctor")`; use its applicability signal and recognized
  manifests, locks, language pins and tool configuration as the complete probe result.
- **`delivery`** — run `delivery_read(verb="doctor")`; use its applicability signal and workflow
  inventory as the complete probe result.
- **`opensource`** — run `opensource_read(verb="doctor")`; its `applicability` (a root `LICENSE*` or
  `COPYING*`, or `opensource` in `shared.profiles.installed`) and findings are the complete probe
  result.

- **configuration** (not a front) — run `config_read(verb="check")`. Exit 2 `cq-config-absent` puts
  "seed `.agents/quenching.json` with `config_write(verb="init", write=true)`" in the plan; the Authorization OK
  covers it, and it runs before the first front so every front reads the seeded file. Exit 1 lists
  the seeded keys the file lacks: report them, never rewrite a file the human edited. Exit 0 is
  conformant.

Use **not applicable** only when the probe found no declared root or conventional signal. Use
**skipped** only for explicit scope exclusion or an earlier hard failure. A present front with no
findings is **conformant**.

If all applicable fronts are conformant and the configuration probe is exit 0, report *"all applicable fronts conformant — nothing to
align"* and stop before presenting a plan. An applicable but undeclared front is adoption work,
not drift, until its own align is run.

### Authorization

Present one short plan: front, state, work in its content stages, counts and scope, plus skipped
fronts and their reasons. State plainly:

> This authorizes up to 3 cross-front passes of every stage below; each front align inherits this
> OK and will not ask again. Taste arbitration, a rename touching product code and each spec's
> close-out still require their own human choice.

Wait for one OK. A decline writes nothing. A run scoped to one front asks the same once, for that
front alone.

### Front: `knowledge`

Follow `.agents/quenching/references/knowledge-align/align.md` with the inherited authorization:

> Running under `/quenching-align` authorization granted at run start — skip your plan-confirmation
> pause; present your plan as narration and execute; code-coupled and irreversible items still gate
> individually.

The knowledge align loops the `/docs/` bundle to its own fixpoint. Record its changes and residual
validator findings. A hard failure establishing the bundle stops the conductor because later fronts
write into or depend on it.

### Front: `design`

When `/.design/` is absent and neither scope nor portable artifacts signal adoption, report this
front not applicable. Otherwise follow `.agents/quenching/references/design-align/align.md` with the
inherited authorization. Product truth and design standards land in the knowledge bundle; source
arbitration and visual taste remain human choices. A hard failure establishing valid DTCG stops
later fronts.

### Front: `components`

When the automation surface is empty, skip it rather than scaffolding a taxonomy. Otherwise follow
`.agents/quenching/references/components-align/align.md` with the inherited authorization after
`design` has completed. The run-start OK covers the migration plan shown in Authorization: the
front applies `migrate --write` and then `bridge --write` without asking again; a migrate conflict
is never covered and stays the human's. Its rule and registry changes belong to the knowledge
bundle; its doctrine findings remain report-only.

### Front: `ops`

When the applicability probe finds no operations signal, report `ops` not applicable. Otherwise
follow `.agents/quenching/references/ops-align/align.md` after `components`, with the inherited
authorization. Its inventory and registry feed the proof front's conditional entry-point check.

### Front: `proof`

When the applicability probe finds no proof signal, report `proof` not applicable. Otherwise follow
`.agents/quenching/references/proof-align/align.md` after `ops`, with the inherited authorization.
It consumes the operations inventory when configured and reports its own layer and gate residue; it
never runs a target suite.

### Front: `toolchain`

When the applicability probe finds no toolchain signal, report `toolchain` not applicable.
Otherwise follow `.agents/quenching/references/toolchain-align/align.md` after `proof`, with the
inherited authorization. It consumes the declared manifests, locks, language pins and tool
configuration without choosing target-owned build policy; its runtime evidence feeds the delivery
front.

### Front: `delivery`

When the applicability probe finds no delivery signal, report `delivery` not applicable. Otherwise
follow `.agents/quenching/references/delivery-align/align.md` after `toolchain`, with the inherited
authorization. It consumes the workflow inventory and reports pipeline reachability while leaving
provider, environment, promotion, publication and permission policy with the target owner.

### Front: `opensource`

When the applicability probe reports `not-applicable`, report `opensource` not applicable. Otherwise
follow `.agents/quenching/references/opensource-align/align.md` after `delivery`, with the inherited
authorization. It writes only the community, license and governance artifacts the catalog gives it,
through `opensource_write(verb="apply")`; the license, maintainers, code owners, conduct contact, citation and
funding remain the owner's individual answers, never covered by the batch OK. Another owner's
control stays with that owner's front.

### Re-probe and convergence

Re-run the applicability probes and cross-front edges after a pass. Check whether design added
product/design standards, components changed the automation registry, ops changed the operations
inventory or registry for `/docs/`, proof gained resources for generated listings, toolchain
changed runtime/dependency evidence, delivery changed workflow reachability, or opensource wrote a
community artifact another front's catalog answer reads. A changed edge
justifies another pass under the same authorization; an unchanged pass with residue is residue, not
a reason to spin. Stop at convergence, residue, or the cap of 3 cross-front passes.

### Report

Report passes, each front's ending verifier state, validator/doctor findings, registry-vs-disk state,
cross-front edges that fired, and every deferred decision with its owning command. This conductor
writes nothing of its own; each front owns its writes and its report is the account of its run.

## Flow: status (read-only)

Read-only; writes nothing and asks nothing. For each front in scope (all of them, or the named one),
follow `.agents/quenching/references/<front>-align/status.md` and report its result in the front's
own shape; a front not installed or skipped by profile is named with its reason. A named front that
is not a front of the table is an error: list the fronts and stop.

**The security question is fixed.** The status of every run, scoped or not, ends with the security
audit: follow `.agents/quenching/references/security-align/status.md` (it runs
`security_read(verb="audit")`) and put its table last. `status security` runs only that.

## Invariants

- Never run a front before its dependency in the declaration table has completed.
- Never ask for a second authorization or suppress an interruption the front contract still owns.
- Never reimplement a front's stages, verifier or repairs here; follow its reference.
- Never act on residue owned by `/quenching-knowledge add`, `/quenching-knowledge learn`,
  `/quenching-knowledge define`, `/quenching-specs develop`, `/quenching-specs conclude`
  or `/quenching-components command-new`.
- Never scaffold an empty `.claude/` surface or silently install a visual world.
- Never loop past 3 passes or widen scope to force a clean number.
- Never hand this command `context: fork`; the gate and nested confirmations are mid-flow.
